name: The Argan of the Orto Botanico

location.address: Orto Botanico di Cagliari, Viale Sant'Ignazio da Laconi 1, Cagliari

access: Paid entry, euro 4 (reduced/free for children under 6, over 65s, disabled visitors and school groups). Open Monday to Saturday, closed Sundays and some public holidays. Same garden and terms as cag_011-013.
transport: In central Cagliari, same site as cag_011-013 (the Moreton Bay Fig, Ombu and Dragon Tree of the Orto Botanico); about a 15 minute walk from the Giardini Pubblici cluster (cag_001-003).
verify_notes: Alive/current: Orto Botanico di Cagliari is confirmed open and operating (sites.unica.it/hbk lists current opening hours, guided visits and ticket prices, checked Sept 2026, prices and hours consistent with cag_011-013's note already on file). Species/rarity: two independent sources both describe this as the only Argania sideroxylon/spinosa specimen in an Italian (and probably European) botanical garden -- apgi.it (Associazione Parchi e Giardini Italiani): 'argan (Argania sideroxylon), unico negli orti botanici italiani'; luoghi.italianbotanicalheritage.com (Italian Botanical Heritage): 'a wondrous specimen of Argania sideroxylon, endemic of Morocco (probably the only one growing in Italian and European Botanical Gardens)'. A third, independent academic source (ricerca.uniba.it, a University of Bari research record on Argania spinosa in Puglia) states as background: 'in Italia l'unico dato riguardante la presenza di piante di A. spinosa fa riferimento ad un esemplare situato nell'orto botanico di Cagliari' (in Italy the only documented A. spinosa specimen is the one at the Cagliari botanical garden). Three independent sources agreeing clears the two-source bar comfortably. Why remarkable/worth the visit: this is the reason to see it, not age or size, but rarity. It is, per two independent horticultural sources, the only argan tree in any Italian or European botanical garden, a species normally confined to semi-arid Morocco and grown almost nowhere else in Europe. No age, girth or planting date found in any source; unlike cag_011-013, no source names this specimen as part of the garden's 1866 founding-era planting, so that bridge is NOT made here (the founding-era age band used for cag_011-013 does not transfer to this tree without its own source). age_estimate and girth left empty rather than guessed; a future visitor or gardener could supply a girth. Location: garden-level precision only, same as cag_011-013 (no source gives an exact bed or path location within the 5-hectare garden); coordinates placed near the garden centre as a placeholder consistent with the other three entries, flagged approximate. Species-match note for a future photo: Argania sideroxylon has small, leathery, oval grey-green leaves and thorny branches, distinct from the broad-leaved fig, the swollen-trunked ombu and the sword-leaved dragon tree already mapped in the same garden, so it will not be confused with them.

name: Dwight's Linden of Finch Arboretum

location.address: John A. Finch Arboretum, Spokane, Washington

verified_sources: https://www.historicspokane.org/spokane-heritage-trees (Spokane Heritage Tree Register; individual record and tree-level coordinate from the city's own ArcGIS layer, CityandCountyHistoricProp/FeatureServer/1, feature 'Dwight's Linden')

https://www.historylink.org/File/10030 (Laura Arksey, 'Spokane's Champion and Historic Trees', HistoryLink.org Essay 10030, 2012, naming this specimen as a champion Hungarian linden at Finch Arboretum planted by pioneer Daniel H. Dwight)
transport: West Spokane, off Sunset Highway; car or city bus. Same site as spk_002 (State Champion White Willow) and spk_003 (First Dawn Redwoods).
verify_notes: Alive/current: on the Spokane Heritage Tree Register's live ArcGIS layer (CityandCountyHistoricProp/FeatureServer/1), same source that verified spk_004-006 this window. Species/age: register names it a Hungarian linden (Tilia x juranyana), age approximately 100 years, height 72 feet, planted by pioneer Daniel H. Dwight, whose family gave Finch Arboretum part of its original ground. Independently corroborated by HistoryLink.org Essay 10030 (Laura Arksey, 2012), which separately names this specimen as a champion Hungarian linden at Finch Arboretum planted by Dwight, citing Dr. Edward Lester's tree survey, the same essay that corroborated spk_004-006. Two independent sources naming the same tree, same planter and same species; clears the two-source bar. Location: garden-level precision from the register's own coordinate, same arboretum as spk_002/003, flagged approximate consistent with those two entries (no more precise fix available). Girth not given by either source; age stated as the register's own figure, held to a decade-wide band rather than repeated as an exact number.

name: The Massive Miyabe of Finch Arboretum

location.address: John A. Finch Arboretum, Spokane, Washington

verified_sources: https://www.historicspokane.org/spokane-heritage-trees (Spokane Heritage Tree Register; individual record and tree-level coordinate from the city's own ArcGIS layer, CityandCountyHistoricProp/FeatureServer/1, feature 'The Massive Miyabe')

https://www.historylink.org/File/10030 (Laura Arksey, 'Spokane's Champion and Historic Trees', HistoryLink.org Essay 10030, 2012, listing Miyabe maple among Finch Arboretum's likely state-first-place champions)
transport: West Spokane, off Sunset Highway; car or city bus. Same site as spk_002 (State Champion White Willow) and spk_003 (First Dawn Redwoods).
verify_notes: Alive/current: on the Spokane Heritage Tree Register's live ArcGIS layer, same source that verified spk_004-006 and spk_007 this window. Species/age: register names it a Miyabe maple (Acer miyabei), a species native to Japan and rare in North American cultivation, age approximately 58 years, height 54 feet, calling it 'a potential state champion'. Independently corroborated by HistoryLink.org Essay 10030 (Laura Arksey, 2012), which separately lists Miyabe maple among Finch Arboretum's likely state-first-place champions, the same essay that corroborated spk_004-007. Two independent sources agreeing on species and standing; clears the two-source bar. Location: garden-level precision from the register's own coordinate, same arboretum as spk_002/003/007, flagged approximate. Girth not given by either source. 'Massive' in the register's own naming refers to relative size for the species (Acer miyabei stays modest compared to the maples people expect), not to the tree competing in scale with the willow or the arboretum's conifers; the story should not overstate its size.
